newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand rollercoastered to a slightly weaker finish on Wednesday after the Finance Ministry removed one of the two uncertainties that have plagued the markets in recent weeks.

After ticking steadily weaker throughout to a day's weakest level of 4.5095 bid by 1400 GMT, a flurry of dollar sales from offshore investors helped the rand recover to 4.5045 bid by 1420 GMT after the Finance Ministry announced limits on amounts local residents can invest offshore.
The Ministry said South African individuals would be allowed to invest 200,000 rand offshore from July 1 when the relaxation of exchange controls, announced in the March 12 budget, are implemented.
Dealers said that the amount was generally in line with market expectations.

"I think in the short-term you can take it as a positive in the sense that it is not a bad amount and the fact that they are going ahead with foreign exchange control relaxations in general," First National Bank chief foreign exchange dealer Dave Sadler said.
"The negative, if there is going to be a negative, will come on July 1 when we see how much funds leaves the country. If not too much leaves than it could also be seen as a positive," he added.
Another senior trader said the limit was at the upper end of the market's expectations, but that the market was taking it in its stride.

"We are seeing some offshore dollars coming in at the moment," the trader said shortly after 1400 GMT. The announcement has removed one of the two uncertainties. The other will be removed once July 1 comes," he said.

Dealers said that on Thursday the rand was expected to remain rangebound between 4.50 and 4.5150 against the dollar, with importer and exporter interest continuing to cap either end of the range and local banks expected to retain their long positions ahead of next Tuesday.

While the market remained uncertain about July 1, dealers noted that fears about an exodus of capital had generally receded in the face of a massive array of reserves and credit lines the Reserve Bank had amassed recently.
Against the crosses, the rand managed to regain some composure against sterling as cable gave up some of the ground it has gained recently.
The rand/sterling cross was last quoted at 7.4979/5058 from a fresh five-month-high of 7.5244 bid posted earlier in the session.
It was also quoted at 0.3822/3828 marks and 25.2462/2965 yen from 0.3827/3832 and 25.4865/5257 respectively overnight.
Bonds also see-sawed throughout the day, initially strengthening in the buildup to the 0900 GMT release of May CPI data before edging weaker in the afternoon in line with the rand.
At 1420 GMT, the key R150 loan yielded 14.50 pct after trading between an intraday low of 14.46 percent and a high of 14.54 percent.
Dealers said there had initially been aggressive foreign buying in the long end of the market, which triggered local short-covering, ahead of the release of the CPI.
When the data came out, beating market expectations of a 9.8 percent year-on-year rise by coming out at 9.5 percent, the market barely moved, leading to some suggestions that the data was leaked.
But a central Statistical Service official said this was unlikely.
"According to our normal security measures it is almost impossible to leak the figure but we will look into the matter," she said.
Later in the day, the R150 ran into profit-taking in the 14.46/47 percent area before it steadily tracked the rand weaker ahead of the foreign exchange annoucement.
One trader said that the limit had been "a bit higher than we thought" but that the market would take its cue in coming days from the rand.
Market players would also look to M3 and credit supply data on Friday for more signs of when interest rates might be cut, the trader added.
On the money market, three-month NCDs dipped below the 16 percent level as the shortage held around the 5.5 billion rand mark.

South Africa's "big four" banks quoted three-month deposit rates at between 15.95 and 15.90 percent offered from 16.00 percent on Tuesday, while the BA rate stood at between 15.50 and 15.35 percent from 15.55 to 15.40 percent overnight.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage little changed at 5.492 billion rand on Tuesday from 5.544 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 171.09 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 227.24 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Tuesday were pegged at 6.64 billion rand from 8.77 billion rand before.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
